people.name: Alexander
people.description: Son of Philip the Macedonian, who came out of the land of Chettiim, smote Darius king of the Persians and Medes, reigned first over Greece twelve years, and at his death parted his kingdom among his servants

people.name: Darius
people.description: King of the Persians and Medes, smitten by Alexander son of Philip, who reigned in his stead

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: King, father of Antiochus surnamed Epiphanes

Surnamed Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king and an hostage at Rome, who reigned in the hundred and thirty and seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks, warred against Ptolemee king of Egypt, entered proudly into the sanctuary at Jerusalem and took away its vessels, set up the abomination of desolation upon the altar in the hundred forty and fifth year, and, after falling sick for grief in Persia and making Philip ruler of his realm to bring up his son Antiochus, died in the hundred forty and ninth year
people.name: Antiochus Epiphanes

people.description: King of Egypt, who fled when Antiochus made war against him and entered Egypt
people.name: Ptolemee
Mattathias
people.description: A priest of the sons of Joarib, son of John the son of Simeon, from Jerusalem, dwelling in Modin, who slew the king's officer and the Jew who came to sacrifice at the idol altar, fled into the mountains with his sons, and on his deathbed charged them to be zealous for the law, naming Simon as their counsel and Judas Maccabeus as their captain

people.name: John
people.description: Son of Simeon and father of Mattathias the priest of the sons of Joarib

people.name: Simeon
people.description: Father of John and grandfather of Mattathias the priest of the sons of Joarib

people.name: Joannan
people.description: Eldest son of Mattathias, called Caddis
Son of Mattathias, called Thassi; named by his father on his deathbed a man of counsel and “a father” to his brethren
people.name: Simon

people.description: Son of Mattathias, called Maccabeus; named by his father on his deathbed as captain to fight the battle of the people; rose up in his father's stead, slew Apollonius and Seron, cleansed and dedicated the sanctuary, campaigned in Idumea, Ammon and Galaad, made a league with Rome, and was killed in battle against Bacchides
people.name: Judas Maccabeus

people.description: Son of Mattathias, called Avaran (surnamed Savaran); died in battle at Bathzacharias after running under a royal elephant and slaying it
people.name: Eleazar

people.description: Son of Mattathias, surnamed Apphus; accompanied Judas his brother into the country of Galaad
people.name: Jonathan
Apollonius
people.description: Gathered the Gentiles and a great host out of Samaria to fight against Israel, and was slain by Judas, who took his sword

people.name: Seron
people.description: A prince of the army of Syria, who went to fight Judas at Bethhoron and was overthrown

A nobleman and one of the blood royal, left by Antiochus to oversee the king's affairs from the river Euphrates to the borders of Egypt and to bring up the king's son Antiochus; twice defeated by Judas, and later slain by the forces of Demetrius
people.name: Lysias

people.description: Son of Antiochus Epiphanes, committed to Lysias to be brought up for the kingdom; set up by Lysias to reign in his father's stead and called Eupator; slain by order of Demetrius
people.name: Antiochus

people.description: Father of Ptolemee, one of Lysias's chosen generals
people.name: Dorymenes

people.description: Son of Dorymenes, chosen by Lysias with Nicanor and Gorgias as a mighty man of the king's friends to go into Juda to destroy it
people.name: Ptolemee

people.description: Chosen by Lysias with Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes and Gorgias to go into the land of Juda; later sent by king Demetrius with great force against Judas, bore deadly hate unto Israel, dealt deceitfully, mocked the priests and vowed to burn the temple, and was slain in battle at Adasa, his head and right hand brought to Jerusalem
people.name: Nicanor

people.description: Chosen by Lysias with Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes and Nicanor to go into the land of Juda; led a night raid against Judas's camp at Emmaus that failed, and later as a captain fought and discomfited Joseph the son of Zacharias and Azarias at Jamnia
people.name: Gorgias

people.description: Captain of the host of the children of Ammon, and later captain of a host gathered against Judas at Raphon, discomfited both times
people.name: Timotheus
Zacharias
people.description: Father of Joseph, whom Judas left as a captain of the people in Judea

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Son of Zacharias, left by Judas with Azarias as a captain of the people and the remnant of the host in Judea; later put to flight with Azarias by Gorgias at Jamnia

people.name: Azarias
people.description: Left by Judas with Joseph the son of Zacharias as a captain of the people and the remnant of the host in Judea; later put to flight with Joseph by Gorgias at Jamnia

One of Antiochus's friends, made ruler over all his realm and charged to bring up his son Antiochus for the kingdom; returned out of Persia and Media seeking to rule the kingdom, and was defeated and taken by the king at Antioch
people.name: Philip

people.description: Father of Demetrius
people.name: Seleucus

people.description: Son of Seleucus, who departed from Rome, took a city of the sea coast and reigned there, had Antiochus and Lysias slain, made Alcimus high priest and sent him with Bacchides against Israel, and later sent Nicanor against Judas
people.name: Demetrius

people.description: Desirous to be high priest, captain of the wicked and ungodly men of Israel who accused Judas and his brethren to Demetrius; made high priest and sent with Bacchides against Israel; trusted by the Assideans as a priest of the seed of Aaron, who then slew threescore of them in one day; contended for the high priesthood and pulled down the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary, and died of a sudden affliction
people.name: Alcimus

people.description: A friend of king Demetrius, who ruled beyond the flood (the Euphrates) and was a great man in the kingdom; sent with Alcimus against Israel, and slew threescore of the Assideans who had trusted Alcimus's oath
people.name: Bacchides
Onias
people.description: High priest at Jerusalem, whose godliness and hatred of wickedness kept the city and the law at peace; reproved Menelaus for stealing temple vessels and was lured out of sanctuary and slain by Andronicus; appeared to Judas Maccabeus in a vision, praying for Israel and presenting Jeremias the prophet

people.name: Jason
people.description: Brother of Onias the high priest; bought the high priesthood from Antiochus Epiphanes and brought Jerusalem to Greek fashions, building a place of exercise and training youth after the heathen manner; undermined in turn by Menelaus and driven out, he later attacked the city, slew his own countrymen, and died in exile after being driven from land to land

people.name: Simon
people.description: Of the tribe of Benjamin, made governor of the temple; fell out with Onias the high priest and told Apollonius the treasury was full of money that could be seized for the king; his faction's hatred led to murders, and his accusations against Onias continued after Heliodorus's failed seizure

people.name: Menelaus
people.description: Brother of Simon and of Lysimachus; sent by Jason to bear money to king Antiochus, he offered more than Jason and got the priesthood for himself, bringing nothing worthy of it; implicated in the murder of Onias and in sacrileges with his brother Lysimachus; later accused Nicanor to Demetrius of favouring Judas, and was at last put to death at Berea for his many sins against the altar

people.name: Lysimachus
people.description: Brother of Menelaus, left by him in the priesthood in his stead; committed many sacrileges in the city with Menelaus's consent, stealing golden vessels from the temple; when the people rose up against him he armed about three thousand men and offered violence, and was killed beside the treasury

people.name: Auranus
people.description: A man far gone in years and no less in folly, who led the people against Lysimachus

people.name: Heliodorus
people.description: Treasurer to king Seleucus, sent to Jerusalem to seize the temple treasury on the report of Simon and Apollonius; struck down and scourged by a horseman and two young men from heaven when he entered the treasury with his guard, and healed after Onias the high priest offered sacrifice for him; he then testified to the king of the mighty power of God at that place

people.name: Hircanus
people.description: Son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, to whom some of the money laid up in the temple treasury belonged

people.name: Tobias
people.description: Father of Hircanus, a man of great dignity, named when Simon misinformed the governor about money laid up in the temple treasury

people.name: Jason of Cyrene
people.description: Author of five books concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brethren, the purification of the temple, the dedication of the altar, and the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and Eupator his son, which this book abridges into one volume

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: Son of Thraseas, governor of Celosyria and Phenice; told king Seleucus of the money in the Jerusalem treasury, which Heliodorus was sent to seize; still governing under Antiochus Epiphanes, he increased Simon's malice against Onias

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: Son of Menestheus, sent into Egypt for the coronation of king Ptolemeus Philometor

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: Son of Genneus, one of the governors of several places who would not suffer the Jews to be quiet and live in peace after the covenants were made

people.name: Andronicus
people.description: A man in authority, left by king Antiochus as his deputy; at Menelaus's urging he deceived Onias with an oath to come forth of his sanctuary and then slew him; for this the king stripped him of his purple, led him through the city, and slew him in the very place where he had killed Onias

people.name: Andronicus
people.description: Left by Antiochus as governor at Garizim, after the Andronicus who slew Onias had already been put to death

people.name: Philip
people.description: A Phrygian by country, left by Antiochus as governor at Jerusalem, more barbarous in manner than the king who set him there; burned a company of sabbath-keepers found hiding in caves near the city; later, seeing Judas increase in strength, wrote to Ptolemeus the governor of Celosyria and Phenice for more aid

people.name: Ptolemeus
people.description: Governor of Celosyria and Phenice, written to by Philip for more aid against Judas's growing strength

people.name: Ptolemeus
people.description: Called Macron; choosing to do justice to the Jews for past wrongs, he endeavoured to keep peace with them; accused before Eupator by the king's friends and called traitor for having left Cyprus, which Philometor had committed to him, and departed to Antiochus Epiphanes, he poisoned himself for shame when he saw he had no honourable place

people.name: Aristobulus
people.description: Of the stock of the anointed priests, master to king Ptolemeus; sent greeting with the council and the Jews of Jerusalem and Judea to the Jews in Egypt

people.name: Demetrius
people.description: King in whose reign, the hundred threescore and ninth year, the Jews at Jerusalem wrote of the trouble that had come upon them since Jason and his company revolted from the holy land

people.name: Eleazar
people.description: One of the principal scribes, an aged man of fourscore and ten years and of a well-favoured countenance; constrained to eat swine's flesh, he spit it out and went willingly to the torment and died, choosing not to stain his old age with hypocrisy, and leaving a notable example of courage to the young

people.name: Posidonius
people.description: One of three men sent by Nicanor to make peace with Judas

people.name: Theodotus
people.description: One of three men sent by Nicanor to make peace with Judas

people.name: Mattathias
people.description: One of three men sent by Nicanor to make peace with Judas; a different man from Mattathias the father of Judas Maccabeus, who had died years before

people.name: Razis
people.description: One of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen and of very good report, called a father of the Jews for his kindness; when Nicanor sent five hundred men to take him, he fell upon his sword rather than be taken, and when his stroke missed he cast himself down from a wall, and at the last, with his bowels in his own hands, called upon the Lord to restore them to him again, and so died

people.name: Rhodocus
people.description: One in the Jews' host who disclosed their secrets to the enemies, and was sought out and imprisoned for it

people.name: Dositheus
people.description: One of Maccabeus's captains, with Sosipater; went forth with him and slew above ten thousand men whom Timotheus had left in a fortress, and together they later took Timotheus himself but let him go for the saving of their Jewish kinsmen he held

people.name: Sosipater
people.description: One of Maccabeus's captains, with Dositheus; went forth with him and slew above ten thousand men whom Timotheus had left in a fortress, and together they later took Timotheus himself but let him go for the saving of their Jewish kinsmen he held

people.name: Dositheus
people.description: One of Bacenor's company, a strong man on horseback, who laid hold of Gorgias's coat to take him alive until a Thracian horseman smote off Gorgias's shoulder and he fled

people.name: Bacenor
people.description: A captain, one of whose company was Dositheus, who nearly took Gorgias alive

people.name: Hieronymus
people.description: One of the governors of several places who would not suffer the Jews to be quiet and live in peace after the covenants were made

people.name: Demophon
people.description: One of the governors of several places who would not suffer the Jews to be quiet and live in peace after the covenants were made

people.name: Nicanor
people.description: The governor of Cyprus, one of the governors of several places who would not suffer the Jews to be quiet and live in peace after the covenants were made; a different man from the Nicanor whom Demetrius later sent against Judas

people.name: Aretas
people.description: King of the Arabians, before whom Jason was accused when he fled from city to city after his failed assault on Jerusalem

people.name: John
people.description: Father of Eupolemus; went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, by whose means the Jews had received royal privileges of special favour, which Antiochus Epiphanes took away

people.name: Eupolemus
people.description: Son of John, who went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, by whose means the Jews had received royal privileges of special favour, which Antiochus Epiphanes took away

people.name: John
people.description: Sent with Absolom from the Jews to deliver a petition to Lysias; a different man from John the father of Eupolemus

people.name: Absolom
people.description: Sent with John from the Jews to deliver a petition to Lysias

people.name: Quintus Memmius
people.description: Ambassador of the Romans, who with Titus Manlius sent a letter of greeting to the people of the Jews agreeing to what Lysias had granted

people.name: Titus Manlius
people.description: Ambassador of the Romans, who with Quintus Memmius sent a letter of greeting to the people of the Jews agreeing to what Lysias had granted

people.name: Chereas
people.description: Governor of the strong hold called Gawra; brother of Timotheus; killed with Apollophanes when the Jews took the city

people.name: Apollophanes
people.description: Killed together with Timotheus and Chereas when the Jews took the hold called Gawra

people.name: Zaccheus
people.description: Left with Simon and Joseph by Maccabeus to besiege two castles in Idumea while he went to places that needed his help more

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Named among Judas Maccabeus's own brethren as a leader of one of his four bands, each of fifteen hundred men; later left by Maccabeus with Simon and Zaccheus to besiege two castles in Idumea. First Maccabees names Mattathias's five sons as Joannan, Simon, Judas, Eleazar and Jonathan, with no Joseph among them; this record follows Second Maccabees' own text rather than resolve the difference

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: One of the priests who made a prayer at the sacrifice when Neemias commanded the wood sprinkled from the rediscovered fire, Jonathan beginning and the rest answering

people.name: Nabuchodonosor
people.description: King of the Assyrians, reigning in Nineve; warred against and destroyed Arphaxad king of the Medes; when the nations of the west made light of his commandment he sware by his throne and kingdom to be avenged upon them, called Holofernes his chief captain and sent him forth with his army to subdue the whole earth and make every nation worship Nabuchodonosor only as god

people.name: Arphaxad
people.description: King who reigned over the Medes in Ecbatane, which he built with massive walls and gates; warred against Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians in the great plain of Ragau, was overthrown with all his power, and was taken in the mountains of Ragau and slain by Nabuchodonosor

people.name: Arioch
people.description: King of the Elymeans; his plain is named among the lands whose peoples joined king Arphaxad against Nabuchodonosor

people.name: Holofernes
people.description: Chief captain of Nabuchodonosor's army, sent to avenge the king upon the nations of the west; mustered a hundred and twenty thousand footmen and twelve thousand horsemen, conquered the nations along the way, besieged Bethulia and cut off its water, heard Achior the Ammonite's report of Israel and had him cast out for it, received Judith in his camp and was deceived by her beauty, and was beheaded by her in his own tent while he lay drunk with wine

people.name: Joacim
people.description: High priest in Jerusalem; wrote to the people of Bethulia and Betomestham charging them to keep the passages of the hill country against the Assyrians; with the ancients of Israel commanded the people, stood before the Lord with the priests offering the daily burnt offerings in sackcloth and ashes during the siege, and afterward came with the ancients of Israel from Jerusalem to see Judith and bless her for what God had done

people.name: Achior
people.description: Captain of all the sons of Ammon in Holofernes' army; when asked by Holofernes told him the true history of Israel and warned that their God would defend them unless they sinned, for which the chief men wished to kill him; Holofernes had him bound and left for the Israelites, who loosed him and brought him to Bethulia before the governors; after Judith slew Holofernes, Achior was sent for, saw the head, believed in the God of Israel, was circumcised, and was joined to the house of Israel from that day

people.name: Ozias
people.description: Son of Micha, of the tribe of Simeon; one of the governors of Bethulia who received Achior from the Israelites, comforted him and made him a feast; during the siege told the people to endure five days and trust God's mercy; was sent for by Judith and approved her words, and blessed God and Judith when she returned with Holofernes' head; sent messengers to the surrounding towns to pursue the fleeing Assyrians

people.name: Chabris
people.description: Son of Gothoniel; one of the governors of Bethulia, present with Ozias and Charmis when Achior was brought to the city, when Judith sent for the governors, and when Judith and her maid went out from the gate

people.name: Charmis
people.description: Son of Melchiel; one of the governors of Bethulia, present with Ozias and Chabris when Achior was brought to the city, when Judith sent for the governors, and when Judith and her maid went out from the gate

people.name: Micha
people.description: Father of Ozias, one of the governors of Bethulia of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Gothoniel
people.description: Father of Chabris, one of the governors of Bethulia

people.name: Melchiel
people.description: Father of Charmis, one of the governors of Bethulia

people.name: Judith
people.description: Daughter of Merari, of the tribe of Simeon; widow of Manasses for three years and four months, fasting and wearing sackcloth in her widowhood; hearing that Ozias had sworn to surrender Bethulia to the Assyrians after five days, she rebuked the people's oath, adorned herself, went out with her maid to the Assyrian camp, was brought before Holofernes, stayed three days in his camp, and on the fourth night, while he lay drunk with wine, took his fauchion and cut off his head; she carried the head back to Bethulia, was blessed by Ozias and all Israel, led Israel in a song of thanksgiving, dedicated Holofernes' goods to the Lord, returned to Bethulia, lived to be a hundred and five years old, freed her maid before she died, and was buried beside her husband Manasses

people.name: Merari
people.description: Father of Judith; son of Ox; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Ox
people.description: Son of Joseph, father of Merari; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Son of Ozel, father of Ox; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Ozel
people.description: Son of Elcia, father of Joseph; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Elcia
people.description: Son of Ananias, father of Ozel; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Ananias
people.description: Son of Gedeon, father of Elcia; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Gedeon
people.description: Son of Raphaim, father of Ananias; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Raphaim
people.description: Son of Acitho, father of Gedeon; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Acitho
people.description: Son of Eliu, father of Raphaim; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Eliu
people.description: Son of Eliab, father of Acitho; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Eliab
people.description: Son of Nathanael, father of Eliu; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Nathanael
people.description: Son of Samael, father of Eliab; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Samael
people.description: Son of Salasadal, father of Nathanael; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Salasadal
people.description: Son of Israel, father of Samael; named in Judith's genealogy, of the tribe of Simeon

people.name: Manasses
people.description: Judith's husband, of her tribe and kindred, who died of heatstroke overseeing the barley harvest at Bethulia and was buried with his fathers between Dothaim and Balamo; left Judith gold, silver, servants, cattle and lands; Judith wore the garments of gladness she had worn during his life and was buried beside him in the cave at Bethulia when she died

people.name: Bagoas
people.description: Eunuch who had charge over all that Holofernes had; at his lord's bidding persuaded Judith to come to the feast; shut Holofernes' tent and dismissed the attendants on the night Judith killed him; the next day found Holofernes dead and headless, and ran out to raise the alarm among the Assyrians
